title: Agent-written tests reshape process and cost more than final outcomes, a study of six models on SWE-bench Verified finds
summary: A preprint by Chen et al. (February 2026) analyses the trajectories of six strong LLMs on SWE-bench Verified to ask whether the tests code agents write on the fly improve issue resolution or mainly mimic a familiar practice while consuming interaction budget. Test writing is common, but resolved and unresolved tasks within the same model show similar test-writing frequencies. When tests are written, they mainly serve as observational feedback channels, with value-revealing print statements appearing much more often than assertion-based checks. In a prompt-intervention study with four of the six models, prompts revised to increase or reduce test writing did not significantly change final outcomes in this setting. GPT-5.2 wrote new tests in only 0.6% of tasks yet resolved 71.8% of them, 2.6 percentage points below the top-ranked Claude Opus 4.5 (74.4%), which wrote tests in about 83% of tasks. The authors conclude that current agent-written testing practices reshape process and cost more than final task outcomes.
source: arXiv Preprint (Chen et al., 'Rethinking the Value of Agent-Generated Tests for LLM-Based Software Engineering Agents')
whyItMatters: If agent-written tests are mostly observational (print statements) rather than assertions, they may leave little regression protection behind, so organizations relying on agents for test coverage should check what the tests actually assert.
Test-writing frequency did not separate resolved from unresolved tasks within a model, so the number of tests an agent writes is a weak proxy for agent capability or code quality.
In this setting the authors found testing shaped process and cost more than final outcomes, which makes the cost of agent-written tests a question worth measuring on your own work.
recommendedActions: Audit the quality and assertiveness of AI-generated tests in your pipelines; distinguish between observational print-based checks and genuine regression-preventing assertions.
Do not use agent test generation volume as a proxy for code quality or agent capability when evaluating AI coding tools.
Keep human-authored test specification and review alongside agent-written code; the study measured issue resolution on SWE-bench Verified, not long-term regression protection.
risksAndCaveats: The study covers SWE-bench Verified issue resolution with an agent where testing is optional, so it says little about integration or end-to-end testing, or about the value of tests for later regressions.
The prompt-intervention experiment used four of the six models, and the work is a preprint; results may differ with other agent designs or newer models.
GPT-5.2's near-zero test writing alongside a comparable resolution rate may reflect strong code generation rather than tests being unnecessary.
